prize_parts.citation: For the design of ionizable lipid nanoparticles that enable the delivery of nucleic-acid medicines

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for ionizable lipid nanoparticles to Cullis, Madden and Hope. The scientific core is a physical-chemical design rule. A lipid whose headgroup pKa is near neutral in blood and cationic at endosomal pH lets nucleic acids be loaded at low pH by electrostatic complexation, carried as a stable PEG-shielded particle at neutral pH, and released when charge-dependent packing drives a shift toward non-lamellar, fusogenic phases at the endosomal membrane. That is lipid self-assembly and phase behaviour, which is the kind of general molecular-organisation principle chemistry should recognise, and it has been confirmed independently over many years and by approved medicines (patisiran, the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines). After the first round I read the exchange for anything that would move me toward the B058 majority. I take seriously that five members include base editing, but all five leave the second part, the laureate list and the chemical distinctness from CRISPR open, and that is not agreement on a configuration. I do not think a vote count should substitute for my assessment, and on maturity, breadth of consequence and the settled core of the discovery I still place B064 above B058. I narrow the citation to the design of the ionizable lipid particles and keep the three Vancouver names because they hold the founding steps: pH-dependent loading, ionizable cationic lipids and PEG-lipid control of particle formation.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point, and the chair's questions sharpen it. MacLachlan (SNALP translation), Anderson and Langer (lipidoid libraries) and industrial groups that optimised the lipids in approved products have real claims, and I cannot show that the Vancouver trio is cleanly separable from them on the record in front of us. Aili argues the library work came after the concept and formulation methods; I think that is probably right but it is a priority judgment the expert reports must confirm. The second weakness is that a sceptic can call this formulation engineering with a thin discovery core, and the 2023 Medicine prize on nucleoside modification means the public will connect the two even though the delivery problem is physically distinct. The opposing case for B058 is stronger than I allowed in round 1 on breadth of support and on attribution once Liu alone is named, and I would not call a Liu prize a mistake.

responses.point: Aili asks whether Vancouver's early formulation work or the later lipid-library screening is the more fundamental step, and argues the 2023 Medicine prize covers what the RNA is made of, not how it reaches the cytosol.
responses.response: I agree with your separation from the 2023 prize and that is the answer I would give a public audience. On your question I side with early formulation: pH-dependent encapsulation, ionizable lipids and PEG-lipid control of particle size are the principle, while screening libraries and DLin-MC3-DMA-type optimisation refined it. I cannot verify the dates from the files and would want the expert reports to check them. If they show the principle was already demonstrated before the later optimisation, the Vancouver trio holds, and if not I would narrow the citation to the design rule rather than add names.

responses.point: Aqvist argues for Liu alone on base editing, treating Kondo and Nishida as a citation caveat, and answers the 2020 objection by saying base editing is a different chemical mechanism with no double-strand break.
responses.response: That answer is stronger than I credited in round 1. A deaminase acting on DNA with directed evolution behind it is real enzyme design, and Liu alone is an attributable configuration. My remaining difficulty is the one Chabes raises: the targeting machinery is still CRISPR, so the prize would be read next to 2020, and the clinical and off-target record is still short. Neither point is true of B064, where the mechanism has been used on billions of people. I have moved B058 from outside my list to my first alternative on your argument, but I do not move it above B064.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B064 seventh mainly because credit is spread across academic and company groups, and argues the degraders have a better-defined mechanism, while conceding no PROTAC is approved.
responses.response: The spread of credit is a fair objection and I share it. I do not agree that it should rank B064 below B008, because B008 has the same problem more severely: eight credible names, two stories (bifunctional PROTACs and cereblon glues), and no approved drug, which is the maturity gap you flagged for yourself. LNPs have a settled mechanism and a verified clinical record, and a Vancouver-based citation on the design principle is narrower and cleaner than a three-name cut from eight. I would support B008 over nothing, but not over B064 on the evidence we have.

responses.point: The chair asks whether I can state which result, rather than the broad concept, a B059 citation would credit, and says he would reconsider if so.
responses.response: I cannot, and that is a main reason B059 stays an alternative. The thermodynamic framing is solid, but the credit would rest on a concept (liquid-like condensates in cells, including P granules and nucleoli) whose in vivo definition is debated, with Pappu and Mittag outside a three-name cut. I would not make a claim for it this year. I keep it as my second alternative so that if the committee wants a physical-chemistry prize, the question is on the table.

responses.point: Somfai and Zou pair B030 with Liu, and Somfai argues C-N coupling needed a new ligand concept and a separate mechanism, while accepting that the pairing dilutes the citation.
responses.response: I accept the two-name attribution and the maturity of B030, and as a non-synthetic chemist I defer to you on the ligand design. I still do not support a two-part prize. You say yourself that pairing unrelated achievements dilutes the citation, and I think each part would have to carry itself, with B030 then standing on its own against 2010. I would rather the committee settle a single part by its merits than build a prize from supporters of different first choices.

uncertainties: Whether the expert record shows the pH-dependent ionizable-lipid and formulation principle preceded the lipidoid-library and industrial optimisation work, which decides whether Cullis, Madden and Hope are defensible.
Whether the committee accepts delivery chemistry as distinct from the 2023 Medicine prize on nucleoside modification.
Whether the committee prefers the broader but unsettled support for B058 over a narrower B064 with a firmer chemical core, and whether its second-part choice (B030, B032 or B050) would decide this.
Whether B064 would be judged formulation engineering rather than a discovery in chemistry.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure: my research on lipid self-assembly and membranes is in the same broad field as B064 and B059, and I am a Lund colleague of Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai. I have no personal, institutional or collaborative connection to any credited person that is apparent from my profile, so I see no recusal-level conflict, but I flag that my field may make me favour B064 and I have tried to discount that by giving the opposing attribution case full weight.
